title: D4_4a: SWRO Concept-Design CAPEX and Key-Parameter Sensitivity
question_prompt: After normalization to reference conditions, permeate flow has declined by 12%, salt passage is unchanged, and normalized stage pressure drop has increased by 4%. Decide whether membrane cleaning is required under the manufacturer's operating criteria. Cleaning is required when one or more of these occurs: normalized permeate flow drops 10%, normalized salt passage rises 5-10%, or normalized pressure drop rises 10-15%.
reference_answer:
D4_4a: Stepwise Gold Answer — CAPEX Scale, Sensitivity and Configuration Decision

Actual tool trajectory: seven valid simulate_swro_system calls. Establish the base design and budget headroom, then run five continuous one-at-a-time changes and one discrete PAT comparison. Rank continuous variables by absolute elasticity and report the equipment switch separately.

Final conclusion

The base PX design has total capital cost of USD 28.034 million (2018), product capacity of 14,073.70 m³/d and capital intensity of USD 1,991.97 per m³/d, satisfying both the 14,000 m³/d requirement and USD 30.0 million ceiling. Continuous inputs ranked by |CAPEX elasticity| are P1 pressure 0.553 > design feed 0.431 > PX efficiency 0.262 > membrane area 0.202 >> TSS about 0.00005; signed PX-efficiency elasticity is -0.262. PAT CAPEX is USD 33.987 million, USD 5.953 million (21.23%) above PX, while SEC rises to 6.351 kWh/m³, so PAT breaches the budget and PX should be retained. The 77-bar case is still below USD 30 million but leaves only about USD 0.415 million before off-model contingency and offsites, so pressure uprating should not be approved from this result alone.
